title: Hive-bee cells form by bees sweeping equal spheres and building at intersections

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hive-bee cells form by bees sweeping equal spheres and building at intersections

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Hexagonal hive-bee cells result from many bees standing at equal distances from one another, each excavating equal spherical hollows, and building up or leaving unexcavated the planes where these spheres would intersect.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The work of construction seems to be a sort of balance struck between many bees, all instinctively standing at the same relative distance from each other, all trying to sweep equal spheres, and then building up, or leaving ungnawed, the planes of intersection between these spheres.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Hive-bee, its cell-making instinct”. Scope: comb construction by the hive-bee (Apis mellifera)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism gives precise measurable predictions and could be cleanly tested. Public data exist for limited colonies and imaging studies, but may not provide adequate replication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Analyze time-resolved imaging and bee trajectories during comb construction for equal spacing, spherical excavation, and wall formation at predicted intersections. Systematic construction by another geometry would refute the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The required time-resolved construction datasets are sparse and scattered.

Wax deformation after deposition can obscure initial geometry.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric prediction is sharp enough to confirm or refute for Apis mellifera, whose comb has been measured many times. Those measurements are not gathered in an open dataset, so a reanalysis means compiling supplements and classic tables. Overlapping predictions from physical models of wax keep the test from cleanly isolating the behavioral story about equal spheres.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare observed cell angles, wall curvature, and bee spacing during construction with the geometry predicted by equal spheres whose intersections are built up. A match to those angles and to equal inter-bee distances would support the mechanism; systematic deviation, or construction kinematics that do not sweep spheres, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cell measurements and construction videos are scattered in papers and are not a public comb database.

Finished-comb geometry does not record the positions bees occupied while building.

Wax rheology and local building rules can produce similar hexagons without bees sweeping equal spheres.
